aAbout: FlightAware tracks flights with a focus on status and operations: live flight status, schedules, airport delay information and flight history, backed by premium accounts that add flight alerts, 3, 5 or 8 months of historical data and saved airports and aircraft. Around the consumer tracker sits a serious aviation-data business — Aviator for general-aviation owners, Global for business-jet operators, FBO Toolbox for airports, and the Firehose data feed for commercial customers.
aStrengths: FlightAware is the deeper tool for what a flight is doing: detailed status and schedules, airport delay and operations information, and a data business that airlines, operators and aviation professionals rely on. Its premium history (3, 5 or 8 months), GA-focused Aviator suite and business-jet Global product serve working aviation in ways an enthusiast map does not try to.
bAbout: ADS-B Exchange is a global platform that aggregates and displays real-time aircraft movements via a collaborative network of contributors, offering a transparent view of the skies without censorship or filtering. Its live Global Map shows all aircraft broadcasts as received — military, commercial and private — fed by what it claims is a network of over 25,000 active receivers, with a map history function going back to March 2020. Alongside the map it sells production-ready enterprise data subscriptions (live and daily position and operations feeds); no enterprise prices are published.
bStrengths: ADS-B Exchange is the deeper tool for what is actually in the sky: an unfiltered, community-fed map that shows military, commercial and private aircraft as broadcast, a history function reaching back to March 2020, detailed aircraft and ownership information, and — by its own claim — positions refreshing every 500ms from over 25,000 receivers. Its personal ad-free tier is also strikingly cheap, and free for the feeders who power the network.
betterAnswer: They solve different problems. FlightAware answers questions about a flight — is it on time, where is it scheduled, what is happening at its airport — and sells that depth to travellers, operators and the industry. ADS-B Exchange answers questions about the sky — what is actually up there, unfiltered, including military and private aircraft other services may not emphasise — and archives it back to March 2020. Check a flight with FlightAware; investigate the airspace with ADS-B Exchange.

faqs.a: They measure different things. FlightAware is generally the stronger source for a flight's status, schedule and airport delay information. ADS-B Exchange shows aircraft positions as broadcast by the aircraft themselves, from a community network it claims has over 25,000 receivers refreshing every 500ms. For position-versus-status, pick the tool built for that question.
faqs.q: Is FlightAware or ADS-B Exchange more accurate?

faqs.a: Yes, by its own description: it displays all aircraft broadcasts as received, with no censorship or filtering, and its store page lists military, commercial and private aircraft among what the map shows. If an aircraft is broadcasting, ADS-B Exchange's stated policy is to show it.

faqs.a: The live Global Map is free with ads. An ad-free personal subscription costs $2.99/month or $29.95/year (personal use only), and people who feed the network get the ad-free map free. Its enterprise data subscriptions have no public price.

intro: FlightAware and ADS-B Exchange track the same sky for almost opposite reasons. FlightAware is the American aviation-data company: flight status, schedules and airport operations are its home turf, with premium accounts for individuals and data products like Firehose for the industry. ADS-B Exchange, founded in 2016 by an aviation enthusiast, is a community-fed network that displays every aircraft broadcast as received — no censorship or filtering — for enthusiasts, researchers and journalists who want the raw picture, military and private traffic included.
pricingA: Free consumer tracking tier with limits and advertising. Premium accounts for individuals add alerts, longer history and saved airports/aircraft; the professional products (Aviator, Global, FBO Toolbox) and data feeds such as Firehose are priced separately for operators and businesses.
pricingB: The live Global Map is free with ads. The personal ad-free subscription costs $2.99/month or $29.95/year — for individual, personal use only, with premium map layers — and feeders get the ad-free map free. Enterprise data subscriptions (Live positions, Live operations, Daily positions, Daily operations) have no public price: ADS-B Exchange does not publish one, so any figure quoted elsewhere should not be trusted.

verdictA: Choose FlightAware if you track for a reason — a specific flight's status, US airport delays, a general-aviation aircraft you operate, or aviation data for a business.
verdictB: Choose ADS-B Exchange if you want the raw, unfiltered sky — military and private traffic included — with deep map history back to March 2020, and you are comfortable with an enthusiast, researcher-oriented map.
verdictLine: FlightAware is the operations desk — status, schedules, delays and industry data. ADS-B Exchange is the raw feed — every broadcast as received, filtered by no one. One tells you what a flight is doing; the other shows you everything that is flying.
worldEye: If you mainly want to glance at the sky rather than work it, WorldEye shows live flights free on a 3D globe — no signup — alongside live ships, satellites, weather, earthquakes, wildfires and 74,229 public cameras across 105 countries in the same view. It is deliberately not a rival to either specialist here: it does not offer FlightAware's status and schedule depth, and it does not claim ADS-B Exchange's unfiltered military data or history back to 2020. An optional Pro tier ($7.99/week, $13.99/month or $74.99/year) adds the OSINT toolkit and intel feeds.
